_about: Rulebook for the Koine voice. Each rule has an id, a layer, what it does, and its basis. Layer 'evidence' = grounded in ancient testimony or documented phonetics; 'interpretive' = a reading choice, switchable off with --no-delivery. Every word in a rendered passage lists the rule ids that touched it.

voice._basis: Public reader (anagnostes) assumed adult male. The neural model is a Modern Greek female voice; Praat shifts formants by 0.86 (adult male vocal tract) and the pitch tier below replaces its melody entirely. noise_w 0 makes durations deterministic so word timings can be measured.

rules.effect: accented syllable +3 semitones over the reciting tone; circumflex rises then falls within the syllable; grave = no rise
rules.basis: Greek accent was melodic: Dionysius of Halicarnassus (On Composition 11) says the speaking voice moves within about a fifth; the accent marks of the Alexandrian grammarians and the Seikilos epitaph (1st c. AD), whose melody follows the accents.
By the 1st c. the pitch accent was turning into a stress accent (loss of vowel length, Koine papyri spellings; Horrocks, Greek: A History of the Language).

rules.effect: pitch drifts down 2 semitones across each breath group
rules.basis: Declination: a near-universal of spoken phrases.

rules.effect: breath group ending in a comma ends on a slight rise (+1.5 st), 0.35 s pause
rules.basis: Suspended cadence at a minor pause, as in the ekphonetic (lectionary) reading formulas, which mark phrase ends with paired cadence signs; pause lengths from the sound model config.

rules.effect: breath group ending in a full stop or raised dot falls 4 st on its last accent, last syllable 30% longer; 0.9 s (stop) or 0.6 s (raised dot) pause
rules.basis: Final cadence (teleia) of the ekphonetic formulas; phrase-final lengthening.

rules.effect: breath group ending in a Greek question mark (;) rises 4 st at the end
rules.basis: Question intonation; the ekphonetic system has a distinct sign for questions in some lectionaries (interpretation of its exact melody is uncertain).

rules.effect: room acoustics from the engine (synagogue hall RT60 about 1.7 s, early stone reflections)
words estimated to be spoken by Jesus: 8% slower, 1 st lower, pitch range x1.1
rules.basis: A reader marking the principal voice with gravity (Quintilian, Institutio Oratoria 11.3, on suiting the voice to the person).

rules.effect: words of other speakers: 0.5 st higher, 3% faster
rules.basis: Distinguishing voices in a dramatic reading (Quintilian 11.3).

rules.effect: 0.25 s extra pause when the speaker changes
verse with weeping/troubled/sorrow words: 15% slower, 2 st lower, range x0.7, -3 dB
rules.basis: Quintilian 11.3: grief makes the voice low, slow and subdued.

rules.effect: verse where someone cries out: +4 dB, +2 st, 5% faster
rules.basis: Quintilian 11.3: a cry raises and strengthens the voice.

rules.effect: verse with joy words: +1 st, range x1.2, 3% faster
rules.basis: Quintilian 11.3: joy makes the voice full and bright.

rules.effect: verse with glory words: range x1.1, 5% slower
verse narrating death or the giving up of the spirit: 20% slower, 3 st lower, -4 dB
rules.basis: Quintilian 11.3: the voice sinks for the gravest matters.
